Contribution guidelines

Clear changes.
Clean history.

Small, focused changes are easier to understand and review. Here’s how we work on the code.

Contribute on GitHub
LINEAR HISTORY

Rebase-only workflow

Keep branches linear and avoid merge commits. Rebase your changes before the final merge.

New to git rebase? Open your pull request. A maintainer can help you squash and rebase the branch.

Example / SDK Multiplayer branch
$git fetch origin
$git rebase origin/Multiplayer

Meaningful commits

Give each commit one purpose. Describe what changed and why, instead of vague messages like “update” or “fixed bug”.

We prefer Conventional Commits. The prefixes are helpful, but not a requirement.

feat:A new featurefix:A bug fixrefactor:Changes to existing codechore:Maintenance tasksdocs:Documentation changes

Maintainer review

Every change needs review from at least one maintainer. We may ask for adjustments to keep the codebase consistent and maintainable.

Ask questions and explain your decisions. Constructive discussion is part of contributing.
